Chapter 5
 1. Describe two ways that the house or regular diet can be
modiﬁ ed to accommodate patient needs.
Another means to modify foods is to add single nutrients 
such as protein through the use of “modular” products. 
Protein modulars, such as ProMod® or Beneprotein®, can 
be added to both foods and beverages but will need to be 
mixed well. Th ere is a slight change in taste and consistency.
3. What are the similarities and diﬀ erences between a clear 
and full liquid diet? When are they used, and what are their 
limitations?
For very short periods (two or three meals), liquid diets 
(clear or full) consisting of broth, juice, cream soups, and
milk may be served to patients who are beginning to eat
after a long period without food. Both diets consist of foods 
that are liquid at room temperature (juice, tea, coﬀ ee, gela-
tin, broth, popsicles), but the full liquid diet begins the intro-
duction of milk products (milk, ice cream, pudding). A clear

residue in the gastrointestinal tract. It may be used during
